COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 1646 of 2026
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Prince Chauhan, learned counsel for
the petitioner.
2. By the instant petition preferred under
Article 227 of the Constitution of India, the
petitioner is praying for the following reliefs:-
(a) To issue a writ order or direction in the nature
of mandamus directing the learned First Addl.
District Judge, Rudrapur District Udham Singh
Nagar to expeditiously hear and decide Civil Appeal
No. 39 of 2026 title as "Gurnam Chandra and
another vs. Rajendra Kumar" within a time bound
period as may be fixed by this Court.
(b) To issue any suitable writ, order or direction
which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in
the facts and circumstances of the case.
As it appears from the relief, as sought by
relief (a) the petitioner is praying for expediting
the Civil Appeal No. 39 of 2026 pending in the
court of First Addl. District Judge, Rudrapur
District Udham Singh Nagar.
3. Now, the brief facts of the case are that the
petitioner preferred a suit, i.e. O.S. No. 121 of
2023, Rajendra Kumar vs. Gurnam Chandra and
another, for permanent injunction against the
defendants who are respondents herein. On
03.05.2023, the Trial Court granted temporary
injunctions by restraining the defendants
including their servants to interfere in peaceful
possession of the plaintiff .
Subsequently, order of temporary
injunctions was challenged by the defendants in
Civil Appeal No. 39 of2026 wherein the learned
Appellate Court directed to maintain status quo.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for
the petitioner that due to the order of status quo

granted by the Appellate Court in Civil Appeal
No. 39 of 2026, the petitioner is unable to sow the
seed in the agricultural land in the current
paddy-crop season which would result in
complete loss of the agricultural yield for current
season.
He further submits that the Civil Court is
now closed for a month due to summer
vacations, and the appeal cannot be expedited
during this current season, therefore, in
alternative that status quo order may be
modified by permitting the petitioner to sow the
seed of paddy-crop in the agricultural land.
5. Admittedly, on perusal of the relief clause
no such relief has been sought by the petitioner
to permit him to sow the seeds but taking into
consideration his alternative prayer, particularly
relief (b), this Court have gone through with the
order of temporary injunction which was passed
by the Trial Court on 03.05.2023 in O.S. No. 121
of 2023. The operative part of the order granted
temporary injunction is reproduced herein as
under:-

On perusal of the order granting
temporary injunctions, the Trial Court recorded
finding that the plaintiff is in possession and that
is the reason that the defendants were restrained
from interfering in the peaceful possession of the
plaintiff.
6. The order of status quo granted by the by
Appellate Court in Civil Appeal No. 39. Of 2026
is of no use particularly when there is a finding
of the Trial Court that the plaintiff is in

possession, therefore, due to the order of status
quo neither the plaintiff nor the defendants can
use the agricultural land.
7. Now this Court under supervisory
jurisdiction is of the view that the order of status
quo should be modified so that the agricultural
land be used for the time being and also keeping
in view the fact that while granting status quo
order, the first appellate court have not stayed
the order of temporary injunction.
Furthermore, the Civil Court are closed
due to summer vacations, therefore, this aspect is
also being considered for the purpose of
modifying the order of status quo.
8. Issue notices to the respondents.
9. Steps to be taken within a week.
10. List this matter on 15.07.2026.
11. For an interim measure, in the peculiar
facts and circumstances of the case the order of
status quo dated 04.09.2025 passed by learned
District Judge in Civil Appeal No. 39 of 2026 is
modified and the petitioner is permitted to sow
the paddy-crop in the land in question which is
admittedly an agricultural land.
12. It is made clear that this interim order will
not come in the way of the Appellate Court while
deciding the Civil Appeal No. 39 of 2026 on its
own merit.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
02.06.2026
Parul
